_headline: Inside the city, NMC's monsoon-2023 readings show dissolved oxygen on the Nag falling from 3.67 mg/L at Ambazari to 0.48 mg/L at its end point. MPCB's 2023-24 index puts the Nag at 75 near Ambazari lake and 36 at Bhandewadi bridge. Below the city, the highest BOD at Agargaon on the Kanhan was 9.8 mg/L in 2023 and 7.4 in 2024.
_excluded: Wainganga stations outside Nagpur district in the same MPCB file (11, 2172, 2173, 2175, 2176).
MPCB state stations 185-189 (national codes 5979-5983): MPCB publishes an index, not readings, and no coordinates; carried in the river notes.
Station 1910 Ambhora: readings kept, coordinate withheld (both official positions are far from the village).

rivers.name: Nag
rivers.cpcb_class: Not assessed: no CPCB readings for the Nag's national-programme stations
rivers.description: The river the city is named after. It flows out of Ambazari lake in the west of the city; 17 km of its course to the Kanhan lie within the city (NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24). The length shown is the stretch drawn on this map. The readings here are NMC's own: one round at ten points during the 2023 monsoon.
rivers.notes: NMC measured dissolved oxygen of 3.67 mg/L at the Ambazari start and 0.48 mg/L at the end point, and faecal coliforms of 80,000 to 300,000 per 100 ml at every site. The report has no BOD column. MPCB's water quality index for its own Nag stations in 2023-24: 75 near Ambazari lake (its Good to Excellent band; MPCB's 2025 national list types this station, 5979, as a lake station), 36 at Bhandewadi bridge and 36 at Asoli bridge (its Heavily Polluted band, 38 and below). MPCB has listed these stations for the national programme as 5979 to 5981; CPCB's river tables up to 2024 carry no readings for them. JICA's appraisal of the Nag project gives a 2019 baseline BOD of 30 to 70 mg/L for river water in the north and central zones. NMC's previous round (ESR 2022-23, Table 6.15, printed p.188) measured BOD of 6 to 49 mg/L at nine points along the Nag.

rivers.name: Pili
rivers.cpcb_class: Not assessed: no CPCB readings for the Pili's national-programme stations
rivers.description: Flows east from Gorewada in the city's north-west and meets the Nag near Pawangaon; 18 km of it lie within city limits (NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, which spells it Pilli). The length shown is the stretch drawn on this map. NMC sampled it at eight points during the 2023 monsoon.
rivers.notes: Dissolved oxygen 4.2 mg/L at Gorewada and between 0.74 and 2.87 mg/L at the seven points below it; faecal coliforms 40,000 to 300,000 per 100 ml. At Pilli-5 and Pilli-6 NMC's table prints more faecal coliforms than total coliforms, which cannot both be right; both are shown as printed. MPCB's index for 2023-24: 45 at Wanjra layout (its Polluted band, 38 to 50); its table shows NA for Mankapur that year (50 in 2022-23). MPCB lists the two stations for the national programme as 5982 and 5983.

rivers.description: The city's third river. It rises near Hingna in the south-west of the city and flows to the south-east (NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24). rivers.notes: Dissolved oxygen fell from 4.8 mg/L at the first point to 0.81 mg/L at the end point; COD reached 56.67 mg/L there. Neither CPCB's station list (file dated 2020) nor MPCB's national-programme list (file dated May 2025) has a station on the Pora.

rivers.name: Kanhan
rivers.cpcb_class: Priority IV in 2025 (II in 2022, III in 2018)
rivers.description: The river the Nag and the Pili drain into. The length shown is the stretch drawn on this map. MPCB samples it every month at three national-programme stations: two at Sinora in Parseoni taluka, either side of the Vidarbha Paper Mills, and one at Agargaon, which CPCB names 'Kanhan D/S of Nagpur'.
rivers.notes: Highest BOD at Agargaon: 9.8 mg/L in 2023 and 7.4 in 2024, against 3.5 in both years upstream at Sinora. MPCB recorded the river at Agargaon as dry in June of every year from 2019 to 2024. CPCB's 2025 report places the stretch from below the Vidarbha Paper Mills to below Nagpur in Priority IV and counts it improved from Priority III in 2018. For 2021 to 2024, MPCB's monthly figures reproduce CPCB's yearly minimum and maximum; for 2018 and 2019 they do not, and CPCB's yearly figures for those years are not shown.

rivers.name: Kolar
rivers.cpcb_class: Priority IV in 2025 (V in 2022, III in 2018)
rivers.description: A tributary that joins the Kanhan at Waregaon in Kamptee taluka, north of the city. The length shown is the stretch drawn on this map. MPCB samples it every month at Waregaon bridge.
rivers.notes: Highest BOD: 7.1 mg/L in 2024. MPCB recorded the river as dry from May to August 2019. CPCB's 2025 report lists one polluted location here, at Waregaon bridge, in Priority IV (V in 2022) and counts it improved from Priority III in 2018. CPCB's 2018 yearly table prints a BOD maximum of 60 mg/L for this station; MPCB's twelve monthly readings for 2018 peak at 18.1 mg/L, so the 2018 yearly figure is not used.

rivers.name: Wainganga
rivers.cpcb_class: Priority IV in 2025 (III in 2022, II in 2018)
rivers.description: The larger river the Kanhan joins east of the city. The length shown is the stretch drawn on this map. MPCB samples it every month at Ambhora, after the confluence.
rivers.notes: No map marker: the official coordinates for station 1910 do not match Ambhora (CPCB's list places it about 145 km to the south, MPCB's about 53 km to the north-west). Highest BOD there: 4.2 mg/L in 2024. CPCB's 2025 report places the Wainganga from below the Ellora Paper Mills in Bhandara to Ashti in Chandrapur in Priority IV.
